narrative:
Your loan application was reviewed carefully, and unfortunately, we were unable to approve it at this time. The decision was based on several key factors in your financial situation that suggested a higher risk of difficulty repaying the loan. Here’s why this happened and what stood out in your application.

First, your current financial stability played a significant role in the decision. The model noted that your checking account balance is negative, which is uncommon among approved applicants—most have at least some savings or a positive balance. Additionally, you’re currently unemployed, and while this isn’t the only factor, it’s a concern because steady income is important for managing loan payments. Most approved applicants have been employed for at least a year, often much longer, which gives lenders more confidence in their ability to repay.

Your credit history was another important consideration. While it’s positive that you’ve paid off all your previous loans with the bank, this is actually quite rare—only about 3% of approved applicants have a similar history. The model may have seen this as unusual, possibly raising questions about why you’ve needed to rely on loans in the past or whether your financial situation has been stable enough to avoid them. On the other hand, your low installment rate (the percentage of your income going toward loan payments) was a point in your favor, as it suggests you’re not overcommitted to other debts.

Other details in your application also influenced the decision. For example, you’ve lived at your current residence for four years, which is longer than average, but you don’t own your home—most approved applicants do. You also have a co-applicant on this loan, which is uncommon and may have added complexity to the assessment. While the amount you requested (1,193 DM) is smaller than the average loan, the combination of these factors led the model to predict a 56% chance of difficulty repaying, which is just above our threshold for approval.

To improve your chances in the future, focus on building stability in the areas that weighed most heavily against you. Rebuilding your checking account balance, securing steady employment, and avoiding new debts could all help strengthen your next application. If you’d like, we can provide guidance on steps to take or resources that may assist you in this process. While this decision isn’t what you hoped for, we want to help you position yourself for success down the road.
